cards.front: How do you give commands in Spanish?
cards.back:
Affirmative tú commands: use the él/ella present tense form (drop the -s from tú form).
Atacar → atacas → ¡Ataca!
Huir → huyes → ¡Huye!
Ustedes commands: use the subjunctive form.
cards.grammarNote: Spanish has separate imperative forms for tú (informal singular), usted (formal singular), nosotros (let's), vosotros (informal plural, Spain), and ustedes (plural). In D&D, you'll mostly use tú commands for direct orders and ustedes for commanding the whole group.
**Ataca** = the tú affirmative imperative of **atacar**. Formula: tú present **atacas** → drop -s → **ataca**. Negative tú command uses the subjunctive: **¡No ataques!** (Don't attack!)

**Huye** = tú affirmative imperative of **huir** (to flee). **Huir** inserts a **y** in conjugation: tú present **huyes** → drop -s → **huye**. Negative: **¡No huyas!** (using subjunctive of **huir**).
**Lanza** = tú affirmative imperative of **lanzar**. Tú present: **lanzas** → drop -s → **lanza**. Note: the preterite yo spelling change (lancé) does NOT affect the imperative.
**Usa** = tú affirmative imperative of **usar** (to use). Regular -ar: **usas** → **usa**. This command is critical in D&D: **¡Usa la poción de vida!** (Use the health potion!) can save a character.

**Cúralo** = ¡Cura! + direct object pronoun **lo** (him/it) attached to the end of the imperative — affirmative commands attach pronouns as suffixes. The accent on **cú-** preserves the original stress: **cura** + **lo** = **cúralo**.

**Defiéndete** = ¡Defiende! (stem-changing e→ie) + reflexive pronoun **te** attached. Accent added to preserve stress: **defiende** + **te** = **defiéndete**. The e→ie stem change applies in the tú imperative.
**Sube** = tú affirmative imperative of **subir** (regular -ir). The tú present is **subes** → drop -s → **sube**. The full phrase **¡Sube de nivel!** (Level up!) is used in Spanish D&D communities.

cards.back:
di (decir) · haz (hacer) · ve (ir/ver) · pon (poner)
sal (salir) · sé (ser) · ten (tener) · ven (venir)
cards.grammarNote: These 8 verbs have irregular tú imperative forms that don't follow the 'drop the -s' rule. In D&D: **¡Ten cuidado!** (Be careful!) · **¡Ven aquí!** (Come here!) · **¡Sal de ahí!** (Get out of there!) · **¡Haz algo!** (Do something!)

**Ten** = tú affirmative imperative of **tener** (irregular — one of the 8). **¡Ten cuidado!** (Be careful!) is one of the most useful phrases in D&D and everyday Spanish. Full phrase: **¡Ten cuidado con las trampas!** (Watch out for the traps!)

Nosotros commands use the nosotros subjunctive form: **atacar → ataquemos**. However, **vamos a + infinitive** (Let's go to / Let's [do]) is more common in everyday speech: **¡Vamos a explorar la mazmorra!** (Let's explore the dungeon!)

Ustedes commands use the ustedes subjunctive form: **atacar → ataquen** (c→qu before e). Jeffrey uses ustedes commands when directing the whole party: **¡Ataquen al dragón!** (Attack the dragon!), **¡Huyan!** (Flee!)

Negative tú commands always use the present subjunctive — never the affirmative imperative form. **muevas** = tú present subjunctive of **moverse** (o→ue: mueva, muevas…). Pronoun placement with negative commands: before the verb (**no te muevas**), unlike affirmative commands where pronouns attach after (**¡muévete!**).

cards.front:
Full battle command sequence:
'Attack! Don't flee! Use the potion!'
cards.grammarNote: Mix of affirmative and negative commands: **¡Ataca!** (affirmative tú) · **¡No huyas!** (negative tú — uses subjunctive **huyas**) · **¡Usa la poción!** (affirmative tú). This is the grammar of D&D combat narration in Spanish.

cards.front: Tell us everything you know. (usted command — to innkeeper)
cards.grammarNote: Usted commands use the subjunctive: **contar** (o→ue) → usted subjunctive **cuente** → **cuéntenos** (with indirect object pronoun **nos** attached). **Todo lo que sabe** = everything you know — **lo que** = what (relative pronoun introducing a clause).
